fields.description: How long a model may sit idle before it is unloaded; 0 means never unload.
Least time an instance is protected from being displaced by other requests.
Longest time an instance is protected from being displaced; must be at least min_hold.
How long a busy model is left alone before a waiting request asks it to drain.
Longest a request may wait in the queue without being given a model.
Longest gap between streamed chunks once a response has begun; 0 disables the check.
Load timeout for profiles of kind command.
Fail a load whose measured upload acknowledges no new bytes for this long; 0 turns the rule off.
How long a clean shutdown waits for in-flight requests before killing children.
How long a forced node may be absent or offline before requests for the profile fail at once.
Most nodes a single model may be split across.
Per-device memory cost added to estimated needs only.
Least memory a node must be able to hold to take part in a split.
Per-instance prompt cache limit on the host.
The llama.cpp server binary started for each model; read once at start because pre-flight probing uses it.
The llama.cpp device name of the local GPU (for example CUDA0).
Command that reports the local GPU's total and used memory.

The node name of the machine the scheduler runs on (no_auto_nodes, exclude_nodes and force_nodes can name it). Used with membership agents; while it is empty, fleet.local_node is used instead. With membership fleet, fleet.local_node is used.

What a profile with force_nodes does when its memory need exceeds the forced nodes' free memory: off, warn (log and start) or reject. With agents, a forced placement that a node's agent would refuse (would_not_fit, or a node whose memory figure is unknown) is refused whatever this says; that refusal cannot be switched off, because such a machine cannot be recovered remotely when it runs out of memory.
Extra share a node of a split model may receive beyond its split fraction (0 to 1).
Margin added to every memory need that is only an estimate (0 to 1).
Cancel a load when a shared-memory node's available memory falls below this; 0 turns the watch off.

Memory reserved on every node of a placement for the growth while the conversation fills the context: this x the profile's context. 0 turns the reserve off; 8 covers what was measured; at most 1024. While on, a stored peak above need share + reserve counts in their place.

Place on the smaller of the latest and the average free memory, and count what is placed or loading on a node at the larger of its reserved figure and what the node measures as used. Off places on the measured free figure.
Flag a node in the node view when its measured use exceeds what is reserved on it by more than this (something else uses memory, or a need is wrong). Never an error.
Margin kept on each shared-memory node, on top of the watchdog floor, when every need on it is measured or a stored peak. 0 keeps the split skew margin.
Margin kept on each shared-memory node, in percent of its share, when the need is an estimate (0 to 50). 0 keeps the split skew margin.
Least margin margin_estimated_percent keeps on a node.

Refuse a placement that does not keep the per-node margin. Off, such a placement starts as a tight fit when weights, context and fill reserve fit with the headroom kept; the margin then only makes Potluck prefer placements that meet it.
Window of a node's average free memory, from its heartbeats; placement_uses_reserved places on the smaller of the latest figure and this average.
How long a worker's upload progress or fleet heartbeat may stay quiet before it counts as silent.
How often a TCP connect probe checks workers; 0 turns it off (leave it off for rpc-server workers).
Let the connect probe run while the instance has a request in flight.
Where the pool's nodes come from: fleet (the fleet console feed) or agents (registrations of potluck-agent). Read once at start.
Ask agent workers to read model files themselves (model_dir in the worker launch); off sends the weights over the worker connection.

The model source a machine made with Create new zone is given when the dialog names none: share:<host>:/<path> (an NFS export the machine mounts), dir:/<path> (a folder on the machine) or push (the weights are sent over the worker connection). Empty (the default): there is none, and creating a zone without a model source is refused. Write it as the new machines reach it.
The agents' memory watchdog floor; a device that shares system memory counts at most the node's available memory minus this.
What a host on a node (profile host: node) takes there besides its device share: added to that node's reservation and taken off its split weight until it is measured.
Start a host on a node with --no-mmap, so its weights count in the node's available memory and the watchdog sees them. Off until measured on hardware.
How long the worker launches of a load may stay starting before the load fails with worker_start_timeout.
Most child log files kept in the child log directory; the oldest are deleted.
Size at which an event history file is rotated.
Most event history files kept; the oldest are deleted.
Newest events held in memory for history queries.
Days the request log (usage.db in the data directory) keeps each request.
Days the request log keeps its hourly totals; daily totals are kept for ever.
Audit entries older than this many days may be pruned by an operator; the application itself never deletes entries (0 keeps everything and is the default).

Central logging (CR-10). Off: no logs object is handed out and the log routes answer 404. It is also off while Potluck has no log store address (LLM_SCHEDULER_LOGS_STORE_URL) and logs_push_url is empty.
How long the log store keeps lines. Passed to the store when it starts.
Most disk space the log store uses; the oldest lines go first. Passed to the store when it starts.
Empty: senders push logs to Potluck's own route. Set (http:// or https://): senders are told this address instead.
Let clients push log lines to POST /api/logs. Off: that route and GET /api/logs/config answer 404.
Most concurrent live (WebSocket) clients.

Ask llama-server for timings on every streamed event ("timings_per_token": true) for /v1 chat and completion streams that do not set it themselves, so a running request shows tokens in and the prefill rate live. Benchmark requests are left as sent. Adds a "timings" key to each event the client receives.

A step of the scheduler's core loop that takes longer than this is recorded (loopSlowStep, at most once a minute) and turns the Scheduler row of the health summary amber. Requests and status reads wait while a step runs.

The default user: the name that signs, in the audit log and the request log, what is done without an access key and without a name of the client's own (the web UI, curl, scripts). There is no login; everyone using the site is this user. 1 to 40 characters, no control characters.

What the models folder may hold. 0 (the default): the health summary judges the real free space of the disks only. Set: it also judges the model files against this budget (amber at 90 %, red when over).
Turn the benchmark feature on or off.
A load this much slower than the baseline run's is flagged as a regression.
Decode tokens per second this much lower than the baseline's is flagged as a regression.
A benchmark run that takes longer than this is stopped and marked failed.

Off by default (0): nothing is removed. When set, a finished, unpinned benchmark run older than this many days is trimmed: its requests and transcripts are removed, the run, its steps and its measurements stay, and the trim is logged. Checked every hour. Preview with GET /api/bench/removals/preview?days=N.
Send recovery requests for hung workers; off means nothing is ever sent. Not used with membership agents.
Recovery actions in escalation order; each may appear once, in the order restart_rpc_server, restart_docker, reboot. Not used with membership agents.
Least time between two recovery requests for one node. Not used with membership agents.
How long a recovery step gets to take effect before the next one is sent. Not used with membership agents.
How long a recovery request stays valid at the node. Not used with membership agents.
Timeout of the request that hands a recovery request to the fleet manager. Not used with membership agents.
Base URL of the fleet console; empty means only the local node is used. Read once when the fleet client starts. Not used with membership agents.
The fleet name of the host the scheduler runs on. Read once when the fleet client starts. With membership agents it is used only while the local_node setting is empty.
Age of the fleet view beyond which remote nodes are not used. Not used with membership agents.
How the profile is started: llama (a llama-server the scheduler places on nodes) or command (a fixed command on the local node).
Model file name under the models directory.
Context size per slot.
Number of parallel slots.
Key-value cache precision; q8_0 and q4_0 need flash_attn.
Turn flash attention on.
Measured memory need; 0 means estimate from the model file (required for kind command).
Tier priorities this profile may use; empty means all.
Node ids or hostnames, in device order, to use instead of automatic placement.

Where the llama-server host process runs: server (the scheduler's machine) or node (the first of force_nodes, started there by its agent; needs membership agents and an agent that offers host_launch).
Explicit split weights, one per forced node.
Extra llama-server arguments appended last; flags the scheduler manages are refused.
Command line containing ${PORT}.
Readiness path polled on the command's port.
Other names that resolve to this profile.
Free text for people: what this profile is for. One line, at most 500 characters; it changes nothing in scheduling.

Marks a profile that a tool generated (a benchmark matrix, a sweep) rather than a person wrote. Lists of models keep such profiles out of the way. Empty means not said: the id decides (bench-*, b-* and m-* count as generated).
Idle unload time for this profile; empty uses the default, 0 never unloads.
Load timeout for this profile; 0 uses the computed default.
Longest gap between streamed chunks; empty uses the default, 0 disables the check.
Fail a load with no acknowledged upload progress for this long; empty uses the default, 0 turns it off.
Case-insensitive hostname glob a node must match.
Fleet role a node must have.
Fleet source a node must have.
True matches only the local host, false only remote nodes.
Platform an agent node must have been given at registration, exact (for example linux-amd64-vulkan). Never matches a node from the fleet feed.
Case-insensitive glob one of the device names an agent node reports must match: a GPU model of its registration or a device of its heartbeat. Never matches a node from the fleet feed.
Tier priority; lower is preferred.
Memory kept free on a node of this tier.
The node's GPU memory is system RAM.
Link speed used to size load timeouts.
How long a node is unusable after an instance releases it.
